body: [{"streamId":"01a18df3-8c1c-76b7-8e0e-5c129a5c62a1","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a18df3-8c1c-76b7-8e0e-5c129a5c62a1\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022Distil hall9k\\u0027s 51 active lessons into fewer, better ones, merging and citing only\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022Every lesson you record here is a merge of lessons already on record, and it cites each one it merged: h9k learn \\u0022\\u003Cthe merged claim\\u003E\\u0022 --distilled-from \\u003Cid\\u003E --distilled-from \\u003Cid\\u003E. The decider refuses a distilled lesson that cites nothing, so there is no way to record a merge without the citations, and that is deliberate.\u0022,\u0022You record nothing this project has not already learned. If reading the inventory gives you a genuinely new insight, that is not this task\\u0027s output: say so in your final summary and let a human decide, rather than recording it here where it would arrive dressed as a merge of things that were actually observed.\u0022,\u0022Each lesson you merged away is retired explicitly, citing the survivor: h9k learn retire \\u003Cid\\u003E --reason \\u0022Absorbed into \\u003Cthe new id\\u003E\\u0022. Merging does not retire anything on its own, and a source left live means the same claim now rides in a prompt twice.\u0022,\u0022A lesson that says one thing nothing else says is left exactly as it is. The goal is fewer lessons that are each worth a prompt\\u0027s line, not the smallest possible number: two claims forced into one sentence teach less than the two did.\u0022,\u0022Your final summary accounts for every lesson in the inventory below under one of three headings: merged into \\u003Cnew id\\u003E, retired as wrong or obsolete with its reason, or left alone. A lesson you did not reach is named as one rather than left unmentioned.\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Spike\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022What kind of task this is. This is a research spike, not a build task: it ends with a findings\\ndocument and no build or test gate, and the platform opens no pull request for it. Recording and\\nretiring lessons with \\u0060h9k learn\\u0060 is this spike\\u0027s work and is not the code a research spike is told\\nnot to write, so do both freely. Name this task on every lesson you record by adding\\n\\u0060--task 01a18df3-8c1c-76b7-8e0e-5c129a5c62a1\\u0060 to the \\u0060h9k learn\\u0060 command: it is what credits the lesson to this run, and\\nwithout it the lesson lands marked as recorded with no run named, which reads to the next session\\nas though a person might have typed it. Put the account of the inventory inside the findings document\\u0027s\\n\\u0022What was observed\\u0022 section: every lesson in the inventory below appears there as merged into a\\nnamed new lesson, retired with its reason, left alone, or not reached, or the section says no merge\\nwas warranted.\\n\\nWhy this task exists: every dispatched session on this project carries a bounded section of its\\nactive lessons, and the section has two caps (a lesson count and a character budget). Past those\\ncaps the oldest lessons stop reaching prompts at all. Retirement is the cheap control and it is\\nalready available to every run; distillation is the other one, and it is deliberately a task a\\nhuman authors and publishes rather than something the daemon decides to do on its own judgment.\\nNothing in this platform distils automatically, and nothing should: merging two claims into one is\\na judgment about meaning, and a wrong merge is worse than two lessons that overlap.\\n\\nWhat \\u0022merge and cite only\\u0022 rules out, concretely. You are not here to improve the wording of a\\nlesson that stands on its own. You are not here to record what you think this project should have\\nlearned. You are not here to generalise three specific observations into one abstract principle\\nthat none of them actually established, which is the failure mode this instruction exists to\\nprevent: the abstraction reads better, survives every review, and is not something anybody\\nobserved. If two lessons say the same thing in different words, merge them and cite both. If three\\nlessons are three faces of one rule that all three genuinely support, merge them and cite all\\nthree. Otherwise leave them alone.\\n\\nHow to read a lesson before you touch it. \\u0060h9k learn show \\u003Cid\\u003E\\u0060 gives you its provenance: which\\nrun and task recorded it, if any, which node it was recorded on, and whether it reaches prompts\\nat all. Read \\u0022recorded with no run named\\u0022 as exactly that and no further: a person typing at a\\nshell records it, and so does an agent that skipped \\u0060--task\\u0060, and nothing on the record separates\\nthe two. A lesson recorded by an agent on another node is rendered in \\u0060lessons.md\\u0060 and held\\nout of prompts pending the security review in idea 7e403b80, so merging one INTO a lesson that\\ndoes reach prompts\\nwould route its claim around that hold. Do not do that: treat a held-out lesson as read-only for\\nthis task, name it in your summary, and leave it.\\n\\nThe live inventory is \\u0060h9k learn list --project hall9k\\u0060, which is what you should actually work\\nfrom. The snapshot below was taken when this task was authored, so treat it as orientation rather\\nthan as the set: lessons can be recorded and retired between then and now.\\n\\nSnapshot taken 2026-10-30 17:55:11Z: 51 active in hall9k, newest first, the first 40 shown.\\n\\n- [28696364] A host-gate 30-minute timeout whose only evidence is stale permit-N.lock.holder sidecars is not by itself a test failure: a touched Docker-backed class that ran 13 to 38 seconds of test time took 450 to 578 seconds wall clock here waiting for permits in /tmp/hall9k-postgres-container-gate held by other sessions, so run each touched class by name, compare its reported Duration with its wall time, and do not change code when every touched class passes and the delay is permit wait.\\n- [06f9a4a4] After true completion stopped clearing the tracker assignee, Decisions Log #223 still says CloseoutEngine.MirrorTrackerReleaseBestEffortAsync clears it at the third holder-release site; that clause is superseded (a finished item keeps its assignee), so do not restore the closeout mirror on the strength of #223, and a human should record a superseding decision.\\n- [68511fa1] To tell who held a run, read RunDispatched alone: NodeId == Guid.Empty AND !IsDeliberateHeadlessStart AND a SessionName that does not end in the build role suffix (h9k task start sets both the sentinel and TaskClaimed.InteractiveMode on a headless build, so neither is the key), and TaskPassageQuery.IsHumanHeld is that one rule; a hand-off point (h9k pr resolve, h9k task handback) is found by the TaskReopened with Automatic false or the TaskHandedBack that precedes a non-human run\\u0027s TaskClaimed, since a PR-stage h9k task drive also appends a non-automatic TaskReopened and is told apart only by the sentinel claim after it.\\n- [a7bd02fb] A closeout test that reads TriageExecutor.Requests right after PollOnceAsync races the background Task.Run CloseoutTriageSessions starts, so wait for the spawn (or WhenIdleAsync when the executor is not HoldOpen) before asserting; the race passes in isolation and can fail deterministically once the class runs in order.\\n- [148b5f54] When a prompt template moves between package directories under .claude/templates (here commit-style.md and review-read-scope.md from agent-prompt-builder to work-prompt-builder), an operator\\u0027s installed override of the old path is orphaned silently, so say so in the handoff; and a pure-string refusal helper (like TaskReleaseCommand.PastPushedTipRefusal) is how a command\\u0027s store-backed refusals get a unit test without a database.\\n- [54d51af9] To resume the conversation a person\\u0027s own session registered, read RunDetails.RegisteredInteractiveClaudeSessionId, never InteractiveClaudeSessionId: the latter moves with every InteractiveSessionStarted, so a contractor h9k task delegate dispatches overwrites it and a resume would land in the contractor\\u0027s conversation.\\n- [32ac0791] A shell-command safety check that unescapes quoting and then matches a refused term (GitReadOnlyGuardRoutes.UnescapeShellQuoting, over raw PreToolUse command text) must reassemble whole shell words the way bash does, not judge each quote or escape in isolation, and even then it still misses expansions that create or split words after quote removal. Reassembly means joining every adjacent unquoted, \\u0027...\\u0027, \\u0022...\\u0022, and $\\u0027...\\u0027 piece between runs of unquoted whitespace into one word, decoding $\\u0027...\\u0027 ANSI-C escapes (bash turns $\\u0027\\\\x75\\u0027 into a literal character before it runs the command), and only then checking whether the whole word starts with the refused term; checking each span alone let --out\\u0027put\\u0027=\\u003Cpath\\u003E, git diff \\u0027--output=/tmp/my file.txt\\u0027, --outp$\\u0027ut=/tmp/my file.txt\\u0027, and --outp$\\u0027\\\\x75\\u0027t=\\u003Cpath\\u003E through, and $\\u0027/etc/passwd\\u0027 reassembles into a literal absolute path. Brace expansion (git diff {/dev/null,~/.config/gh/hosts.yml} reads the file; git diff -{-output=/tmp/x,-stat} writes it) and unquoted $IFS word splitting (git diff --output${IFS}/tmp/x) still bypass a reassembling guard, so refuse any git diff/log command whose text contains an unquoted \\u0027{...,...}\\u0027 or a \\u0027$\\u0027 expansion outside a fully single-quoted word, or better, allowlist the argument shapes a lens needs instead of denylisting spellings one at a time. Any future unescape-then-match check on command text should be built this way from the start rather than adding one quote form at a time.\\n- [88f9f51a] To name the node an owner-act request or hold actually lives on, use TrustedOwner.ResolveRootActingNodeId (K0\\u0027s node first, which h9k project members marks (root)), not RootNodeDescription.Of: the latter names the newest rotation\\u0027s holder (marked (root key)), so after any succession rotation the two point at different nodes.\\n- [be3bdfbc] When scrubbing an incident\\u0027s identifiers from the tree, search for its bare pull-request numbers too, not only the names: test method names (Replaying_\\u003Cnumber\\u003E_...) and FluentAssertions because-strings (\\u0022...on PR #\\u003Cnumber\\u003E\\u0022) carry incident numbers that a name-pattern grep never matches.\\n- [a175d0d8] When renaming fixture names across tests, a stand-in must sort the same way as the name it replaces (project lines are ordered by name, so a test that expects the stand-in first fails if it sorts after hall9k) and must not contain a word a test asserts is absent from rendered text (a login containing \\u0027review\\u0027 broke a NotContain(\\u0027review\\u0027) check); the default no-Docker gate does not run the RequiresDocker integration classes, so run each touched one scoped by name with a FullyQualifiedName filter.\\n- [2b83a214] On the Mac, a gate\\u0027s wall-clock span includes lid-closed sleep and the gate timer counts awake time only; check pmset -g log before calling a gate overrun or killing its process by PID\\n- [48418886] A background task that appends to a task stream with no expected version races closeout polls and sibling background tasks over the same stream, and Marten throws EventStreamUnexpectedMaxEventIdException for the loser, so reload the aggregate and retry a bounded number of times instead of dropping the write; and a test double that records spawn requests from concurrent sessions needs a lock around its List, or an add is silently lost and a one-per-key assertion flakes.\\n- [7c1c956b] An owner\\u0027s go on a GitHub comment pinned only by its node id does not pin its text: review comments and review bodies stay editable forever, and a session told to read \\u0027comment X by id\\u0027 reads whatever X says now. Pin an approval to what the owner saw by carrying a copy of the body (as the admitted-review path does) or by recording lastEditedAt / a body hash at hold time and refusing the read when it changed.\\n- [63ae102d] A unit test of ClaudeExecutor\\u0027s spawned command must not assert it starts with the literal \\u0022claude\\u0022: other tests in the same process set HALL9K_CLAUDE_PATH, so the binary part is a fake-claude.sh path whenever they overlap; assert on a stable flag such as \\u0027 -p --output-format stream-json \\u0027 or on the wrapper prefix instead.\\n- [6cc71858] A CLI command that prints untrusted multi-line text (a PR comment body, an issue body) beneath its own structural header lines (Comment N by \\u003Clogin\\u003E:, Status:, Thread N:) must fence each body with RelayedText.Fenced(RelayedText.Printable(body)), the way ReviewLapPromptBuilder.Fenced does; folding only the one-line fields to OneLine still lets the body print forged header rows that misattribute text to another login or fake a thread status.\\n- [cf41e5c6] When a change widens who the replication receive gate refuses for a Conditional task act (e.g. reading the assignee instead of the creator for TaskPublished/TaskRevised), check that every CLI command appending that act runs TaskOwnerGuard first: h9k task publish and h9k task revise carry no owner guard at all, so a Member-role sender the gate now refuses still appends locally and its own node forks from every peer (the drop is permanent when origin == sender).\\n- [2377a581] An acceptance criterion asking for the whole host suite\\u0027s own before/after timing, measured with the host gate\\u0027s own command, cannot be satisfied from inside a dispatched build session: AGENTS.md\\u0027s working rules forbid running dotnet test with no filter (the host gate\\u0027s own full command) from here, with the sole exception being a single touched test class scoped by name. When a card\\u0027s acceptance criteria and AGENTS.md\\u0027s own working rules point in different directions on how something must be measured, AGENTS.md wins: report the touched-class timing you can measure directly, and state plainly in the PR that the full-suite number needs the daemon\\u0027s own host gate run rather than fabricating or extrapolating it as though it were measured.\\n- [6ab6853e] A pre-flight-style gate that reads attacker-controllable content through two separate CLI calls to the same external tool (gh pr diff --name-only then gh pr diff, or any read-twice-and-compare pattern) cannot be made race-free by rereading and retrying around it, because the tool\\u0027s own response never says which underlying commit/state it actually read; the only race-free fix is to pin the read to an explicit, named identifier in the request itself (e.g. GitHub\\u0027s compare API with an explicit base...head, rather than gh pr diff\\u0027s implicit \\u0027whatever the PR\\u0027s head currently is\\u0027). Found in RunLauncher.DispatchPrReviewPreflightAsync (independent pre-PR review, cycle 5, adversarial lens).\\n- [8be8b68c] A background monitor that can end without reaching a real verdict (timeout, budget exhaustion, launch failure, a dead process at restart) must mark its own row with a distinct terminal marker, not merely leave its own completion field null \\u2014 a gate that reads null-completion alone as still in flight, or a sweep that re-processes an incomplete row without excluding one already handled, loops forever with no fresh attempt ever dispatched again.\\n- [57835971] A gh subcommand\\u0027s own minimum version (when it first shipped, e.g. gh attestation verify at 2.49.0) is not the same floor as the flags a caller actually passes to it (--source-ref/--signer-workflow needed 2.68.0, cli/cli#10308); a too-old-gh detector matching only the wording for an unrecognized subcommand (\\u0027unknown command\\u0027) misses a gh new enough for the subcommand but too old for a flag, which fails with \\u0027unknown flag\\u0027 instead \\u2014 match both wordings and quote the flag-driven floor, not the subcommand\\u0027s first-shipped version, in messages/help/docs.\\n- [06a7910b] A CLI command whose confirmation prompt needs to be driven from a test (interactive y/n vs non-interactive refuse) should reuse Hall9k.Cli.Infrastructure.IInteractiveConfirmation / ConsoleInteractiveConfirmation / Tests.Fakes.FakeInteractiveConfirmation, the existing seam OwnerPromoteCommand already uses, rather than inventing a parallel AnsiConsole.Profile.Capabilities.Interactive check: it is directly discoverable via that one existing consumer and keeps every interactive-confirm command testable the same way.\\n- [62a14459] A Windows host-gate timeout whose verify-host.log goes silent right after TaskHolderClaimTests\\u0027s own Skip block, with its per-run gate-wait-host directory empty, is not CrossProcessContainerGate permit contention: TaskHolderClaimTests\\u0027s PostgresFixture is never constructed when every one of its own tests is Skip-attributed (confirmed: dotnet test --filter on that class alone finishes in 26ms with zero container start). The silence has to be a different Postgres-backed class\\u0027s own Testcontainers container start hanging past its 5-minute ContainerStartTimeout without the CancellationToken actually unblocking it and without ever throwing the DockerApiException/Testcontainers marker GateInfrastructureFailureClassifier looks for, so it reads as a bare 30-minute timeout with nothing to classify. Reproduced twice on PR #636 (task 53ffc224) with the identical symptom on two separate host-gate runs; every individually-scoped class this PR\\u0027s diff touches (unit and Docker-backed) passed in seconds both alone and combined, ruling out this PR\\u0027s own commits as the cause.\\n- [1808724b] A prompt-builder test that isolates one line with prompt.Split(\\u0027\\\\n\\u0027)[0] must TrimEnd(\\u0027\\\\r\\u0027) the result before measuring its length: StringBuilder.AppendLine writes Environment.NewLine, so on Windows that segment still carries the trailing \\u0027\\\\r\\u0027 of its own \\u0022\\\\r\\\\n\\u0022, inflating length-bound assertions by exactly one character only on that OS. Windows-only PR #636 CI failure in AgentPromptBuilderTests\\u0027s spike-heading-length test was this, not a flake.\\n- [66e98a3f] A pr-review task\\u0027s agent context must keep WorkItemContext.CarriesQuotedDescription true: AgentPromptBuilder\\u0027s adopted-external-item, QaReviewPromptBuilder\\u0027s basis-is-data and DesignReviewPromptBuilder\\u0027s context-is-data rules key on WorkItemContext\\u0027s exact NonInstructionFraming sentence, so any new composer that quotes stranger text (e.g. AutoPrReviewEngine.ComposePrReviewContext) with different framing prose silently drops those platform-authored data-only rules; reuse the sentence or widen the detector, and pin it with a test.\\n- [14c63c2d] FakeLedger.WriteAsync never throws LedgerPushRejectedException or InvalidOperationException, it only returns a Conflict outcome on blob-id mismatch, so a command\\u0027s catch-after-throw escalation branch (e.g. NodeRevokeCommand\\u0027s WriteRevokedSuccessorAsync catch) is untestable through FakeLedger alone; when the failure condition is knowable in advance (e.g. by comparing TrustedOwner.RootKeys rank before writing), prefer a check-before-write design over relying on the write to throw, since only the former is directly testable with the existing fakes.\\n- [25c83b84] AutoPrReviewEngine\\u0027s two pr-review mint paths (CreateOneAsync, CreateFromMentionAsync) now build agent context through AutoPrReviewEngine.ComposePrReviewContext, not WorkItemContext.Compose, so a pull request\\u0027s attacker-authored title on a public repository sits inside the same fence as the body rather than on WorkItemContext.Compose\\u0027s own unfenced title line; leave WorkItemContext.Compose itself untouched for every other import type (h9k task add --from-pr, --from-issue, --from-jira) since those are human-confirmed before an agent ever sees them.\\n- [ccc37c9c] ClaudeSettingsFile.BuildForPrReview built its mention-answer.md Write() permission rule with Path.Combine(runDirectory, \\u0022mention-answer.md\\u0022), which emits a backslash on windows-latest CI and breaks the rule (Claude Code\\u0027s permission-rule format is forward-slash only, same as every other AbsolutePathRule() in that file) - windows-latest is the only CI leg that catches a Path.Combine used inside a forward-slash-only string being built elsewhere in the same method with plain string interpolation; grep ClaudeSettingsFile.cs and similar permission/settings-string builders for Path.Combine before trusting them cross-platform.\\n- [f059f669] A prefix allow rule Bash(git diff:*) is not read-only-within-the-checkout: git diff with any path outside the working tree (e.g. git diff /dev/null ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml) silently switches to --no-index and prints that file\\u0027s content, and git log/diff do not accept abbreviated long options (--outp= is refused), so --output is the only write flag to guard but --no-index/outside paths are a read escape that Read/Grep path scoping does not cover.\\n- [3d94121a] UnverifiedLedgerWriteDecider.Observe previously threw DomainValidationException when RootFingerprint was blank, but the \\u0027ref\\u0027 kind MessageSweepEngine.WithAppendOnlyExactRefIntegrityAsync and GitLedgerChainReader\\u0027s members/owner/node ref refusals all deliberately pass an empty RootFingerprint for a ref with no single owning root (records, members, prompt-addenda, run-skill) - every such refusal threw and was silently swallowed by the sweep\\u0027s own catch block, so it never once reached h9k status until the validation was relaxed to allow a blank root fingerprint. Also, git show-ref --verify --quiet exits 128 (not the ordinary 1) the moment a ref\\u0027s own commit object is missing locally, so a bool ref-exists check built on it can never distinguish \\u0027missing object\\u0027 from \\u0027ref truly absent\\u0027 - for-each-ref --format=%(refname) \\u003Cexact-ref\\u003E is the correct existence probe since it never resolves the target object.\\n- [b196e3c0] Any test helper that appends ProjectSettingsChanged/ProjectTeamSettingsChanged with non-empty VerifyCommands and then actually exercises DispatchEngine.ClaimEligibleAsync or VerificationRunner.VerifyAsync/VerifyForSettlingAsync must also append a matching ProjectGateSetAccepted for that same list in the same seed (GateSetAcceptance.Decide holds otherwise) - VerificationRunnerTests.SeedAsync, SpikeEngineTests.SeedClaimedSpikeAsync, and six sites in ReviewEngineTests.cs all needed this fix; a plain grep for \\u0027verifyCommands: Optional\\u003CIReadOnlyList\\u0027 across tests/ combined with checking whether the same test file calls VerifyAsync/ClaimEligibleAsync is the fast way to find every site.\\n- [56f86714] dotnet test --results-directory \\u003Cpath\\u003E run against Hall9k.slnx from the repo root (as ci.yml\\u0027s ubuntu Test step does) writes blame/results output directly under \\u003Cpath\\u003E as one GUID-named run folder, not per test project, so an actions/upload-artifact step with path: \\u003Csame path\\u003E (no glob needed) captures --blame-hang\\u0027s Sequence file and mini dump; verified locally by running the exact flags added to .github/workflows/ci.yml (--blame-hang --blame-hang-timeout 10m --blame-hang-dump-type mini --results-directory ./TestResults) against the full suite.\\n- [bc66af41] EventReplicationOutbox resolves each event\\u0027s project LIVE at flush time (ReplicationProjectResolver on the stream\\u0027s current state), so after h9k idea assign moves an idea from project X to Y, the move AND any of that idea\\u0027s earlier events not yet flushed ride Y\\u0027s outbox, arriving at a receiver that still holds the idea under X. Any inbox-side project-ownership check must treat an idea stream crossing projects as potentially legitimate (EventReplicationInbox.EvaluateCrossProjectIdeaEvent checks the sender against the SOURCE project\\u0027s own ledger chain) rather than refusing on ProjectId mismatch alone.\\n- [3e3d7b43] In EventReplicationInbox relay tests, a forwarded Task/Run act now needs a genuine EventCatchUpRequest (ForStreamId = the task id, Candidates = [], addressed as MessageAudience.Node(receiverNodeId) with about = requestId.ToString()) to pass IsForwardedRecordAdmitted before it ever reaches the Task/Run act classification gate; EventCatchUpResponder.ResolveRequestedStreamIdsForAdmissionAsync always includes the requested stream id itself even when the requesting node has never seen that stream yet (a fresh-genesis catch-up ask), so ForStreamId is a valid admission shape even for a relayed genesis.\\n- [ddfafcdd] Hall9k now generates a per-install Postgres password (32 CSPRNG bytes as 64 lowercase hex, PostgresRuntime.GeneratePassword) instead of shipping the public \\u0027hall9k\\u0027 constant; Hall9kDatabase.DefaultConnectionString is gone, replaced by ConnectionStringWithPassword(password) plus an internal LegacyDefaultConnectionString/IsLegacyDefaultConnectionString pair used only to detect a pre-migration config.json. DatabaseDoctor.MaybeMigrateLegacyPasswordAsync migrates an existing install on the first \\u0027h9k doctor --yes\\u0027 that runs with the daemon stopped, over one Npgsql transaction (ALTER ROLE with a precomputed SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier via ScramSha256PasswordVerifier, then config.json, then COMMIT), guarded by the same ownership check as task 359e0d7a\\u0027s port-binding recreate. This is a binding decision a human needs to record with \\u0027h9k decide --supersedes \\u0022Decisions Log #118\\u0022\\u0027: h9k decide record itself refuses from this dispatched, unattended run (\\u0027a decision recorded from inside a run needs a human attending\\u0027).\\n- [dadda959] In GitLedgerCommitReader.ReadCommitsTouchingPathAsync, a trailer-less (pre-trailer) commit that is TREESAME to its parent for one path is ambiguous between \\u0027never touched this path\\u0027 and \\u0027deliberately reasserts this path\\u0027s already-current content\\u0027 - git tree diffing alone cannot tell them apart, since both produce an identical tree entry for that path. The safe disambiguator is whether the commit\\u0027s WHOLE tree (every path, not just the one being checked) is byte-identical to its parent\\u0027s: a true no-op commit changed nothing anywhere, so unlike an ordinary owner write to some other real path (the cycle-5 laundering scenario), there is no actual content change in it to launder the queried path through, making it safe to treat as touching every path including the one being queried.\\n- [3ec737b2] A daemon sweep engine test that seeds a node via NodeBootstrapSeed.NewNodeAsync gets no OwnerDetails.RootFingerprint at all, since bootstrap never claims one; any new owner-role gate keyed off OwnerRootFingerprintResolver.ResolveAsync (like PromptAddendaSweepEngine.PushAsync\\u0027s own gate) needs the test\\u0027s own seed step to append OwnerDecider.ClaimRoot for that owner and build a matching FakeLedgerChainReader TrustChain (an Owner-role ProjectMember at that fingerprint), the same pattern MessageSweepEngineTests already uses, or every existing push-path test silently starts failing its own Owner-role check.\\n- [ad0727c5] A raw NpgsqlConnection OpenAsync (DatabaseReachability.ProbeAsync, SchemaPresentAsync) uses Npgsql\\u0027s default pool, and Npgsql 9\\u0027s PoolingDataSource.CheckIdleConnector only checks IsBroken and lifetime, never socket liveness, so after hall9k-postgres is recreated or restarted inside the same h9k process an idle pooled connector to the dead container opens with no I/O and reads as Reachable; the first real query on it then throws \\u0027Exception while reading from stream\\u0027. Any probe meant to prove a freshly (re)started Postgres ready must use Pooling=false or call NpgsqlConnection.ClearAllPools() after the container action. Verified by decompiling Npgsql 9.0.4 with ilspycmd.\\n- [19c5368a] To find unused using directives in this repo, temporarily append \\u0027[*.cs]\\u0027 and \\u0027dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0005.severity = warning\\u0027 to the root .editorconfig, then run \\u0027dotnet build tests/Hall9k.Tests -p:EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true -p:GenerateDocumentationFile=true --no-incremental\\u0027 and grep the output for IDE0005; restore the .editorconfig afterward. \\u0027dotnet format style --diagnostics IDE0005 --verify-no-changes\\u0027 exits clean and prints nothing here even when unused usings exist, so its silence proves nothing.\\n- [ddc8ecf7] Claude Code\\u0027s settings.json effortLevel key accepts only low, medium, high and xhigh \\u2014 never max. Verified against the installed binary (2.1.282) by grepping its Mach-O for the settings schema: effortLevel:G([\\u0022low\\u0022,\\u0022medium\\u0022,\\u0022high\\u0022,\\u0022xhigh\\u0022]).optional().catch(void 0), while the sibling maxEffortLevel key takes the five-name list including max, and the binary\\u0027s own help text says \\u0027max is session-only and is not written\\u0027. The .catch(void 0) means an out-of-enum value is swallowed silently: no warning, the key resolves to undefined, and the session runs at the model\\u0027s own default. Only the --effort CLI flag and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL accept max. Before shipping any knob that writes a Claude Code settings key, grep the installed binary for that key\\u0027s own zod schema rather than assuming the documented CLI vocabulary matches the file vocabulary.\\n- [7a81f6ce] To reproduce an h9k install or update path from a dispatched session, isolate it with HALL9K_HOME plus HALL9K_CONNECTION_STRING at a scratch database AND clear HALL9K_DISPATCHED_RUN_ID in the child\\u0027s environment: DispatchedSessionInterceptor refuses install/update/uninstall on the run-id variable alone, with no regard for whether HALL9K_HOME points anywhere near the live install, so the scratch run is refused exit 70 before the command starts.
